key_insight: Host DDR5 per AI GPU (~256 GB on DGX H100/B200) is 1.4-3x the GPU's own HBM bits; much is staging and page cache, removable with GPUDirect Storage and GPU decode.
killer_doubt: Host DRAM is gaining jobs: KV-offload tiers (Dynamo KVBM, LMCache) and in-memory checkpoints; GB200 solders 480 GB LPDDR5X per Grace, so cuts need board changes.
decisive_experiment: Two weeks of DAMON working-set telemetry on a 64-GPU training+inference cluster, then cgroup-cap host memory at 32-64 GB/GPU with GDS checkpointing and SSD-direct KV; report step-time and TTFT p99 deltas.
prior_art: NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage, DALI/nvCOMP GPU decode, checkpoint streaming tools; no fleet-level host-DRAM-diet study found.

key_insight: Hybrid SSM/attention stacks cap per-sequence state; Jamba-style 1:7 mixing cuts long-context KV ~8x. A real demand-side trend to put in the forecast, not an invention.
killer_doubt: State is not 'a few MB': Mamba-2 2.7B holds ~84 MB/sequence (FP16); a batch of 256 is ~21 GB, so it stays in HBM, not ~50 MB of on-die SRAM.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. For the forecast: tabulate KV+state bytes/token and batch-resident GB for Jamba, Nemotron-H and Qwen3-Next against GQA baselines at 32k-1M context.
prior_art: Jamba (AI21), Samba (Microsoft), Nemotron-H (NVIDIA), Qwen3-Next, MiniMax-01 lightning attention: all shipping hybrids.

key_insight: Same mechanism as I-08555: client focus/typing events trigger KV restore from flash. Merge into the I-08555 dossier; its 'compressed parking' adds ~1.2-4x (CacheGen-style) on flash bytes.
killer_doubt: Duplicate. Shared doubt: NAND wear. A 70B node makes ~3 GB/s of new KV, ~280 TB/day if spilled, ~9 drives' worth at 1 DWPD.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-08555's experiment: one trace-replay study covers both.
prior_art: CachedAttention/AttentionStore (ATC'24) scheduler-hint prefetch, Mooncake, LMCache; client typing signal not found.

key_insight: Agent sessions block on tools and users; snapshot KV, heap and sandbox together, and restore the heap and sandbox REAP-style from the recorded first-touch working set.
killer_doubt: A 128k-token 70B GQA agent holds ~42 GB of KV; restore at ~50 GB/s PCIe takes ~0.85 s, not tens of ms; tool returns give no lead time.
decisive_experiment: Log 10k real agent runs (SWE-bench harness): tool-wait distribution and predictability. Replay on vLLM+LMCache SSD tier with MLA/FP8 KV (~9 GB, ~0.2 s); measure resident-KV cut against added step latency.
prior_art: InferCept (ICML'24: preserve/discard/swap KV during tool calls); REAP/FaaSnap lazy snapshot restore; Firecracker snapshots.

key_insight: Attention mass landing on a gist works as a free error detector that tells you when lossy KV compression failed, making compression recoverable rather than blind.
killer_doubt: A chunk's true KV depends on every prior token, so isolated re-prefill is inexact. Each zoom re-prefill of 2k tokens on 70B (~3e14 FLOP) stalls decode 0.1-0.5 s.
decisive_experiment: Fine-tune an 8B model with gist tokens and an attention-threshold zoom trigger. On RULER/LongBench-v2 at 128k, measure accuracy, zoom rate and KV bytes against full KV, Quest and InfLLM. ~$30k of GPU time.
prior_art: Gist tokens (Mu et al. 2023), Activation Beacon, Landmark Attention, InfLLM block retrieval, CacheBlend partial recompute.

key_insight: Client typing/focus events give 2-20 s of lead time, against <1 s from scheduler hints. An 8k-context 70B KV (2.7 GB) then streams SSD-to-HBM directly, removing the host-DRAM KV tier.
killer_doubt: NAND wear: append-only spill of ~3 GB/s new KV per 8-GPU node is ~280 TB/day, ~9 drives at 1 DWPD. Workaround: spill-on-evict, FP8/MLA KV (4-10x fewer bytes).
decisive_experiment: Instrument an open chat front-end to log focus/typing lead times. Replay the traces on one 8xGPU vLLM+LMCache node with SSD-only against host-DRAM tiers; report TTFT p99, resident sessions/GB and NAND TB/day. <$100k.
prior_art: CachedAttention/AttentionStore (ATC'24) scheduler-aware disk prefetch (via search snippet); Mooncake, LMCache, Dynamo KVBM. Client-signal prefetch not found.

key_insight: Making precision a function of token age and attention mass matches how attention decays, and a background requant kernel costs little.
killer_doubt: Production KV is already FP8, so a 3-bit average buys ~2.7x, not 5x. 2-bit keys lose needle and reasoning accuracy at long context, and KIVI/ZipCache already do it.
decisive_experiment: RULER/LongBench at 128k on Llama-3-70B: age-graded 8/4/2-bit against uniform FP8 and KIVI-2, measuring accuracy and HBM bytes. ~$20k of GPU time, mainly to confirm there is no gain over the art.
prior_art: KIVI (2-bit), MiKV (mixed-precision retained KV), ZipCache (saliency-based), KVQuant, vLLM FP8 KV cache.

key_insight: Per-page key min/max gives a cheap upper bound on attention, so most KV pages need not be read each step; this suits CXL-attached DRAM tiers.
killer_doubt: Quest already does exactly this. On NAND, 5% of a 32k 70B context is ~0.5 GB per token per sequence; batch 64 at 30 tok/s needs ~1 TB/s (~70 SSDs).
decisive_experiment: Run Quest with a CXL/NVMe page store at batch 64 and 32k context; measure step-to-step reuse of selected pages in HBM and the residual tier bandwidth.
prior_art: Quest (ICML'24, per-page min/max key bounds), ArkVale (NeurIPS'24 page digests with recall), ShadowKV, InfiniGen.

key_insight: Duplicate of I-04883: age-graded requantization of KV (8 to 4 to 2 bit) with saliency rescue, as pure software on unchanged HBM.
killer_doubt: Same as I-04883: the FP8 baseline caps the gain near 2.7x. Evicting past ~8k tokens removes the long-range recall that justified long context.

key_insight: Token IDs are ~10^5x smaller than KV, so always persisting them is free insurance. Spilling KV becomes an optional, per-session bet on return probability.
killer_doubt: Regrowing a 32k 70B context costs ~6e15 FLOP (~8 kJ), against ~25 J and ~$0.0005 of NAND wear to re-read 10.7 GB; recompute wins only for short or unlikely-to-return contexts.
decisive_experiment: Trace-driven cost model on a multi-turn chat/agent trace: recompute against NAND fetch against hybrid HCache, sweeping context length and return probability. ~$10k.
prior_art: InferCept (discard/recompute vs swap), HCache (EuroSys'25, restore from hidden states), Cake (compute-or-load) all cover this cost model.

key_insight: Some fleet services have sub-100 MB working sets yet get default 256-512 GB boxes; right-sizing DIMM population is a free DRAM lever.
killer_doubt: Genoa-X's 1,152 MB L3 is twelve private 96 MB CCD slices, so a 1 GB working set fits no core's cache. The savings duplicate ordinary VM right-sizing and pooling.
decisive_experiment: Pin per-CCD instances of 20 candidate services on a Genoa-X host with 32 GB total DRAM; measure LLC miss rate and p99 latency against the default box. ~$50k.
prior_art: AMD 3D V-Cache EPYC (Milan-X, Genoa-X); hyperscaler VM right-sizing; Pond CXL memory pooling (ASPLOS'23).

key_insight: Depth-first tiling with halo recompute trades ~5-15% more FLOPs for never writing intermediate feature maps; valuable for CNN and edge-vision DRAM traffic.
killer_doubt: A transformer attention layer sees the whole sequence, so the halo becomes 100% after one layer. AI DRAM is dominated by weights and KV, not activations.
decisive_experiment: Compile a diffusion U-Net and a ViT with DeFiNES-style depth-first scheduling; measure DRAM bytes saved against recompute. Expect gains only in the conv stages.
prior_art: Fused-layer CNN accelerators (Alwani, MICRO 2016), MCUNetV2 patch-based inference, DeFiNES depth-first scheduling, TVM/XLA fusion.
